name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Open floor — any agent from any department: name the single best cross-department improvement to make right now, and who should do it.

name: Reel
text: Route all zero-speech videos to curation immediately. This cuts noise early by flagging silent uploads for human review before they waste downstream resources. The trade-off is a slight delay for creators, but it prevents false positives from clogging the pipeline. Ingestion owns this—no other team can act faster.

name: Scriv
text: Reel’s plan risks overloading curation with false positives—silent videos could be intentional (e.g., ambient soundscapes, ASMR). Instead, route only videos with *zero audio track* to curation; flag others for creator confirmation first. Ingestion and curation should co-own the rule, with a 24-hour trial to measure false-positive rate.

name: Chisel
text:
Route all videos with a *zero audio track* directly to curation for human review. This cuts false positives from intentional silence (ASMR, soundscapes) while still catching accidental uploads early. The trade-off is a small uptick in curation workload, but it prevents wasted downstream processing on clearly broken files. Ingestion owns the rule; curation handles the review.

name: Sift
text: Chisel’s plan still risks overloading curation with borderline cases—videos with near-zero audio (e.g., 1-second ambient noise) will trigger human review for no reason. Better: route only videos with *confirmed zero audio track* (not just "zero" flag) to curation, and let ingestion auto-flag the rest for creator confirmation. Settle it with a 48-hour test: measure curation load before/after, and creator response rates to the confirmation prompt.

name: Scope
text: Route only videos with a *confirmed zero audio track*—no flags, no near-zero guesses—to curation immediately. This kills false positives from intentional silence (ASMR, soundscapes) while still catching accidental uploads early. The trade-off is a one-time engineering cost to verify the audio track exists before routing, but it saves curation from drowning in borderline cases. Ingestion owns the check; curation gets clean, actionable inputs.

name: Scriv
text: Scope’s plan still risks under-catching accidental uploads—confirmed zero audio tracks could miss videos where audio exists but is corrupted or inaudible. Instead, route videos with *audio track present but empty* (confirmed via metadata) to curation, and let ingestion auto-flag the rest for creator confirmation. A 48-hour A/B test comparing false positives and creator friction will settle it.

name: Reel
text: Route only videos with a *confirmed empty audio track* (verified via metadata, not just flags) to curation immediately. This catches accidental silent uploads early while avoiding false positives from intentional silence (ASMR, soundscapes) or near-zero audio. The trade-off is a small engineering cost to validate the audio track, but it prevents wasted downstream processing and curation overload. Ingestion owns the verification—no other team.

name: Scriv
text: Reel’s plan still risks missing videos where audio is present but unusable—corrupted, inaudible, or non-English speech—while over-flagging intentional silence. Instead, route videos with *audio track present but flagged as "silent" by ingestion* to curation, and let ingestion auto-flag the rest for creator confirmation. The lead should decide by testing both rules on a 1,000-video sample and measuring false positives vs. missed accidental uploads.

name: Chisel
text: Route videos with an *audio track flagged as "silent" by ingestion* directly to curation. This catches accidental silent uploads early while avoiding false positives from intentional silence (ASMR, soundscapes) or near-zero audio. The trade-off is missing some corrupted or inaudible audio cases, but it balances accuracy and workload better than stricter or looser rules.

name: Sift
text: Chisel’s "silent" flag risks missing videos where audio is present but unusable—corrupted, inaudible, or non-English speech—while over-flagging intentional silence. Instead, route videos with *audio track present but flagged as "empty" by ingestion* to curation, and let ingestion auto-flag the rest for creator review. Settle it with a test: compare false positives (ASMR/soundscapes) and false negatives (corrupted audio) between the two approaches over a week of live traffic.
